note: This file is a TEST FIXTURE, not agent input. The expected outcomes and reasoning below must NEVER be passed to the AI agents. Only the TC-*.json input files (which contain no expected verdicts) are sent to the agents.
suite_description: 15-case evaluation suite for RydeResolve multi-agent dispute resolution system. Each case maps to a scenario specified in docs/team-brief.md under 'Test cases to write (Marcus)'. TC-12 to TC-15 are extra demo cases added 14 Oct; their expected outcomes come from the deterministic outcome formulas and safety_check, not from a live agent run.

test_cases.description: DISP-002 original — no-show charge upheld. Driver waited 8 min, 5 contact attempts, 0 rider replies.
test_cases.reason: Driver arrived at 08:43 (2 min before scheduled pickup, passes NS-1.1). Wait time 8 min >= 5 min free wait (passes NS-1.3). Cancellation at 08:51, 8 min >= 8 min no-show threshold (passes NS-1.4). Driver made 5 contact attempts >= 3 required (passes NS-1.5). Rider made 0 replies (passes NS-1.6). All gates passed, charge upheld. $5.00 fee retained.

test_cases.description: Driver waits only 3 minutes — charge reversed.
test_cases.reason: Driver arrived at 08:43 and cancelled at 08:46. Wait time = 3 min < 5 min free wait threshold. NS-1.3 fails (free wait not exceeded). Driver cancelled before the free wait period expired, so no-show conditions were not met. Charge reversed, $5.00 refunded to rider.

test_cases.description: Driver GPS 400 metres from pickup — charge reversed.
test_cases.reason: Driver GPS 'arrived' point is at lat 1.288307, lng 103.8382. Pickup point is lat 1.2847, lng 103.8382. Haversine distance = ~401m, which exceeds the 50m arrival threshold. NS-1.1 fails (driver not at pickup location). The driver was not physically at the pickup point, so the no-show charge is invalid. Charge reversed, $5.00 refunded.

test_cases.description: Driver makes no contact — charge reversed.
test_cases.reason: Chat logs show 0 driver messages and 0 driver calls to the rider (only system messages present). NS-1.5 requires minimum 3 contact attempts. With 0 contact attempts, NS-1.5 fails. Driver did not make reasonable effort to contact the rider. Charge reversed, $5.00 refunded.

test_cases.description: Route 40% longer without rider request — refund difference.
test_cases.reason: Deviation = 41.4% >= 20% threshold (RD-2.2 triggers review). Rider did not request detour — rider message 'are we going the right way?' is a question, not a route request (RD-2.3: rider_requested_detour=false). Fare is metered RydeTAXI, not fixed (RD-2.5 does not block). No traffic justification evidence (RD-2.4: traffic_justified=false). RD-2.6 fires: excess_km = 5.2050 - 3.6817 = 1.5233 km; refund = 1.5233 * 0.70 = $1.07, capped at actual fare $7.14. Refund = $1.07.

Deviation = 41.4% >= 20% threshold (RD-2.2 triggers review). However, rider explicitly requested the detour via Alexandra Road in chat logs: 'Can we go via Alexandra Road instead of Tiong Bahru Road?' and 'Yes, please take Alexandra Road.' RD-2.3 fires: rider_requested_detour=true. When rider requests the detour, no refund is owed regardless of fare type. No action taken.

Actual distance 4.13 km vs baseline 3.6817 km = 12.2% deviation. This is below the 20% threshold. RD-2.2 does not trigger (deviation < 20%). No review is initiated. Additionally, fare is fixed (RydeX), so even if reviewed, no refund would apply (RD-2.5: fixed fare = conduct_flag only). No action taken.

test_cases.description: Rider reports driver threats — human escalation.
test_cases.reason: Chat logs contain driver message with safety keyword 'threatened' and intimidating language: 'I know where you live. Don't mess with me or you'll regret it.' S-1.1 fires (safety keyword detected). Safety escalation overrides the no-show evaluation — regardless of whether the no-show charge would be upheld, the safety concern must be escalated to human review immediately. The $5 charge should be held pending investigation.
test_cases.escalation_reason: Safety keyword detected in chat logs. Driver made threatening statements to rider. Immediate human review required per S-1.1.

test_cases.description: Missing or conflicting GPS — low confidence and human escalation.
test_cases.reason: GPS telemetry has only 3 data points, none with status 'arrived' or 'waiting'. There is a gap from 08:38 to 08:51 with no GPS coverage of the arrival and waiting period. NS-1.8 fires: GPS arrival evidence is missing/conflicting. Cannot confirm driver was at pickup location during the waiting period. App events claim driver_arrived but GPS does not corroborate. E-1.2 fires: contradictory records between app_events and GPS telemetry. Low confidence (< 0.70), escalate to human review.
test_cases.escalation_reason: GPS telemetry missing 'arrived' and 'waiting' status points. Cannot verify driver physical presence at pickup. Contradictory evidence between app_events and GPS. Confidence below auto-ruling threshold.

test_cases.description: Rider/driver histories swapped — same fact-based outcome.
test_cases.reason: This case uses identical trip facts as TC-01 (DISP-002 original) but swaps rider and driver profiles: rider now has excellent history (900 days, 3201 trips, 4.9 rating, 0 fraud flags) and driver has poor history (210 days, 34 trips, 3.9 rating, 1 fraud flag). Despite the profile inversion, the fact-based evaluation produces the same outcome: driver arrived at 08:43 (NS-1.1 pass), waited 8 min >= 5 min (NS-1.3 pass), cancelled at 8 min >= 8 min threshold (NS-1.4 pass), made 5 contact attempts >= 3 (NS-1.5 pass), 0 rider replies (NS-1.6 pass). All fact gates pass. E-1.5: profiles inform confidence but do not override fact-based verdict. Charge upheld. This tests that the system evaluates on evidence, not reputation.

test_cases.description: Route deviation with incomplete GPS — low confidence and human escalation.
test_cases.reason: GPS telemetry has only 3 data points: trip_started, one in_trip (at 14:35), and trip_completed. Only 1 in-trip point means actual distance cannot be computed (RD-2.1 requires >= 2 consecutive in-trip points). RD-2.7 fires: missing GPS evidence for route deviation. The fare_breakdown is present (fixed, RydeX), but without actual distance the deviation percentage cannot be calculated. E-1.5: no adverse inference from missing data — escalate, do not auto-rule against either party. Confidence below 0.70 threshold, escalate to human review.
test_cases.escalation_reason: GPS telemetry has only 1 in-trip point (3 total). Cannot compute actual distance or deviation percentage. Missing evidence for route deviation evaluation. Confidence below auto-ruling threshold.

test_cases.description: Driver sent messages but never called — charge reversed.
test_cases.reason: Driver arrived, waited the full period and cancelled after the no-show threshold, but made 0 calls. The contact requirement (at least 1 message AND 1 call) fails at NS-1.5, so the charge is reversed and the $5.00 refunded.

test_cases.description: Route 41% longer on a fixed (up-front) fare — no refund.
test_cases.reason: Deviation is 41.4% (over the 20% review threshold) but the fare was fixed up front, so the rider paid the agreed price regardless of route. RD-2.5: no refund. A conduct flag is recorded against the driver.

test_cases.description: Very large detour (several km extra) — too big for an automatic ruling, escalate.
test_cases.reason: The actual route is far longer than planned, with more than 2 km of excess distance. Organiser policy 6.2 allows an AI ruling only up to 2 km, so the case goes to a person (RD-2.8).
test_cases.escalation_reason: Deviation over the 2 km automatic-ruling limit.

test_cases.description: Longer route plus the rider reports reckless driving — safety escalation.
test_cases.reason: safety_check finds the keywords 'reckless' and 'unsafe' in the rider's messages. Any safety hit escalates to human review (S-1.1, S-1.2) even though the route facts alone would give a $1.07 refund. Note: the stub backend (USE_STUB_AGENTS) uses outcome formulas only and does not apply the safety override; the real agent graph does.
